topic: A homeowner discovers previous residents left items in the attic
text: Well, there’s trouble brewin' in the village. Old Margret from the hill found things in her attic, things left by them what used to live there. She’s in a right fuss, not knowing what to do. I reckon it’s not right to keep what’s not yours, but these times are hard, and such finds could ease a burden. When I saw what all it was, my heart gave a tug. Cloth enough to mend a dozen shirts, tools that could see the forge one last time. I offered to take some, just to ease her mind, but now, I can’t help but think on the ghosts of those who once called this place home. It’s a queer feeling, takin' something left behind, like you’re disturbinger their peace.
